messages:
maria: FYI - we're seeing a persistent backlog of tiny GPU pods pending in us-east1 since ~09:30 UTC. pods request 0.25 A100 equivalents and prefer 'gpu-shape=high-bandwidth'. scheduler keeps skipping nodes with mixed gpu types and leaves small slots unused.

devin: is this the fractional-gang class again? last time it was warmpool config. any obvious taints/affinity blocking?

maria: attaching a quick kubectl pull:

```
$ kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | egrep "tiny|pending"
train-tiny-aaa  0/1 Pending  0  18m  (nodeAffinity=preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: gpu-shape=high-bandwidth)
train-tiny-bbb  0/1 Pending  0  16m  (nodeAffinity=preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: gpu-shape=high-bandwidth)
```

$ kubectl get nodes -l gpu-shape -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,SHAPE:.metadata.labels.gpu-shape,FREE_GPU:.status.allocatable.gpu
node-a100-1  high-bandwidth  0
node-l4-12   high-efficiency  2
node-mix-09  high-bandwidth,high-efficiency  1
```

leo: looks like nodes with mixed labels are treated as incompatible because the scheduler's shape-scoring plugin currently requires exact match on the preferred label when gang scheduling is in play. tiny pods are 'preferred' not hard, but the plugin has a bug: it zeroes score for multi-label nodes when affinity contains a single label.

ops-bot: ALERT: us-east1 pending tiny-pods > 300 (threshold 50) at 2025-08-07T09:32Z.

devin: ok that explains pass-over behavior. mixing of labels is common after rolling in cheaper L4 machines. scheduler should consider label superset matches as valid for tiny pods.

maria: mitigation options: (A) quick contact: mark mixed nodes as gpu-shape=high-bandwidth (lies) for scheduling-only (fast), (B) change scheduler plugin to accept superset matches (dev work), (C) create a tiny-nodepool with uniform A100s and drain/cordon the rest (costly + slow), (D) make tiny pods accept high-efficiency shape via a feature flag (possible perf regression). thoughts?

leo: (A) gets pods scheduled fastest but risks placing on nodes with different perf. we can add a node annotation so telemetry flags allocations that came from relabeled nodes. (B) is correct long-term: change behavior to treat labels as matching if node labels superset requested labels OR if node has a label group that maps to equivalent shapes. scheduler PR should be small if we expose the label-match function.

maria: temporary schedule: enact (A) on non-prod first then prod if metrics look ok. also run perf tests to validate that tiny jobs on mixed nodes don't spike latency.

defin: cost note: if we create dedicated tiny-nodepool (C) we'll add ~20% monthly GPU cost for reserved warm capacity. prefer (A) + (B) roadmap.

scheduler-bot: SUGGESTION: create feature-flag "shape_superset_match" in the shape-scoring plugin. toggle=false by default. telemetry: emit when pod scheduled onto node with superset-match.

maria: agreed. immediate steps:
- leo: submit small scheduler PR to allow superset label match (target: v0.42.1)
- devin: run relabel playbook to mark mixed nodes as high-bandwidth in us-east1-np1 (non-prod) -> test schedule
- ash: add perf test harness for tiny pods on mixed nodes
- ops-bot: open ticket INFRA-2033 for follow-up and cost analysis

leo: PR opened: github.com/redwood/eng-platform/pull/4921 - implements superset-match with unit tests. requesting review.

devin: relabel job ran on non-prod pool (20 nodes). after relabel, pending tiny pods dropped from 320 -> 18 in 6m. no obvious perf anomalies in traces.

ash: ran 30-minute perf run on mixed nodes (tiny pods). 95th latency increased ~6% vs pure A100, median unchanged. tagging as acceptable for non-critical workloads.

maria: rolling relabel to prod is scheduled in 30m during low traffic window. will monitor pending queue & eviction churn.

ops-bot: ACTION_CREATED: INFRA-2033 "shape superset scheduling + tiny-pod relabel experiment" assigned to devin, leo, ash. ETA 3d.

devin: longer-term: add a node attribute 'gpu-capability-score' numeric and use scoring functions instead of brittle labels. also evaluate binpacking plugin to coalesce tiny pods using fractional allocation.

leo: yep. RFC: "shape-aware packing: numeric capacity and topology hints". I'll draft for next week.

maria: postmortem threshold: if pending tiny-pods > 100 after relabel + superset feature enabled, we'll escalate to paging. otherwise keep as follow-up work. :rocket:
